messages:
maria_gonzalez: Heads-up — I noticed the model card examples for `stratus-legacy` vs `stratus-v2` show different token counts for the same prompt. This is causing the SDK snippet in the migration guide to be misleading (users see different token bill). Can we coordinate a quick docs PR to reconcile examples and add a compatibility note?

noah_kim: Yup, saw this in the perf runs too. The tokenizer change in v2 (+BPE tweaks) adds ~+1-3 tokens on short prompts. We should: clarify supported tokenizers in the card, add a short "tokenization notes" section, and update the SDK snippets to show explicit tokenization.

iris_docs: I can open the PR. Plan: update model card example prompts, add a one-paragraph migration note, and update the Python/JS SDK examples to use explicit tokenization calls. Will also add a tiny benchmark summary (median token delta) so readers see the impact.

samuel_lee: If you update snippets, please make sure both python and js snippets reflect the current SDK surface. JS uses `client.encodePrompt()` in examples now; python has `client.tokenize()` in v3.2. We'll need to run the docs snippet validator (docs-ci) before merging.

ben_platform: From infra side: recommend we add a short "pin variant" note under Dedicated/Dedicated+Private sections. If customers auto-upgrade between variants they can see different token costs unexpectedly. Also add a link to the compatibility matrix. (Also pinging: docs-bot link-check might catch broken links.)

docs-bot: Link-checker: found 1 broken link in docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/model-compat (404) — reported 3078904560.

ben_platform: Ah, yeah that's the old internal path. Correct public doc is https://console.redwood.ai/docs/model-compat. I'll open a redirect ticket for the old path.

maria_gonzalez: For the snippet changes, propose adding this explicit tokenizer example in the card: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
print(client.tokenize("Hello, world"))  # show token ids + count
``` and a short JS counterpart: ```js
const client = new RedwoodClient();
console.log(await client.encodePrompt("Hello, world"));
``` Also call out that embeddings are computed on post-tokenized sequences and may differ if tokenization changes.

iris_docs: Drafting PR now — question: do we want a small benchmark table in the card (1 row) showing avg token delta across common prompts (e.g. "user prompt set A")? Or just a single-line summary like `avg +1.8 tokens`?

noah_kim: Single-line summary is fine for the card (keeps it lightweight). Link to a longer bench file in the model catalog repo for those who want full numbers. Also add a migration checklist snippet: 1) run token-diff tool, 2) pin model variant, 3) retest prompt quality & token usage. We'll add the token-diff tool link.

samuel_lee: Token-diff tool lives at https://git.redwood.dev/tools/token-diff — I'll add a short example output in the PR. Reminder: when updating snippets, run `npm run docs:snippets` and the python snippet validator. I can run those in CI after you push.

iris_docs: Will link to token-diff and include example. Also adding a small unit-test in docs that asserts example token counts stay under the documented limit (so future regressions get flagged).

maria_gonzalez: Ok assigning reviewers: @noah_kim and @samuel_lee. Target merge by EOD tomorrow (need this for the release notes).

samuel_lee: sgtm, I'll validate snippets against SDK v3.2.0 and run the docs CI when the PR is up.

maria_gonzalez: Great — thanks all. I'll follow up once PR is opened. :thumbsup:
